idea-plugin.name: GenAI PHP Portable
idea-plugin.description:
Write & run PHP code in IntelliJ IDEA Community for free. PHP Portable is a lightweight, feature-rich way to add PHP support to the free IDE — no PhpStorm license and no system-wide PHP install required.

Minimal PHP support for IntelliJ IDEA Community (which does not bundle the paid PhpStorm language plugin):
  • Portable PHP SDK — download a portable PHP interpreter from inside the IDE (like the JDK downloader); no system install required.
  • Run PHP script — a run configuration that executes a .php file with the selected PHP SDK or an explicit interpreter path.
  • Syntax highlighting — lightweight, lexer-based highlighting for .php files (tags, keywords, strings, comments, variables, numbers).
This is an MVP; semantic features (completion, go-to-def, inspections) are a later step, best delivered by wrapping a PHP language server via LSP4IJ.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.16
  • File icon now matches current PhpStorm (New UI): the blue "php" glyph with an automatic dark-theme variant, taken from the platform's New UI icon set. Replaces the old-UI file-sheet icon from 0.2.15.
0.2.15
  • The .php file icon is now the official PhpStorm PHP file icon (from the JetBrains PHP plugin, Apache 2.0, copyright header preserved), so files look exactly like they do in PhpStorm.
0.2.14
  • The .php file type no longer sets a custom icon — files render with the IDE's default file icon.
0.2.13
  • Fixed: remaining red tabs/project-tree marks on files using protobuf accessors or env-variant config classes. Those marks come from RAW ERROR-severity diagnostics (Wolf marks), which client-side filtering cannot touch. worse.missing_member — the provider behind both the protobuf __call accessor and the variant-class constant false positives — is now disabled by default at the source. All remaining ERROR-severity diagnostics are gone, so no file gets marked. Set language_server.diagnostic_ignore_codes yourself to re-enable (the plugin's protobuf/variant class filtering then still narrows the noise).
0.2.12
  • No more protobuf false positives and style noise on legacy codebases.
    • A stub for the runtime-provided \ProtobufMessage base class is installed with the PHP stubs, so inherited methods (parseFromString, serializeToString, …) resolve instead of being reported as missing.
    • Generated protobuf message accessors (getIdKeys, …) are provided by the runtime's __call magic — the remaining "Method … does not exist" findings on extends \ProtobufMessage classes are now suppressed (the class list ships with the generated class map).
    • Style diagnostics that are pure noise on legacy code — worse.docblock_missing_param, worse.docblock_missing_return_type, worse.missing_return_type, worse.undefined_variable — are disabled by default via the maintained Phpactor config. Set language_server.diagnostic_ignore_codes yourself to override.
0.2.11
  • Fixed: diagnostics pipeline crashed with LSP4IJ 0.21.0 — it bundles lsp4j 1.0.0, where Diagnostic.getMessage() returns Either<String, MarkupContent> instead of String. The plugin's filter (compiled against the older signature) threw NoSuchMethodError, killing LSP4IJ's whole diagnostics pipeline — stale editor marks, tab underlines and project-tree error badges could never be cleared. Message access is now version-proof (reflective) and any failure degrades to "no filtering" instead of breaking the pipeline.
  • PHP file icon is now the classic PHP logo (ellipse + php) instead of the custom monospace mark.
0.2.10
  • Fixed: false "Class not found" still marked tabs and the project tree red. Editor and Problems view were clean, but file tabs and the tree kept the red marks — those come from Phpactor's diagnostics pipeline, which runs in a configuration context that never receives the plugin's LSP settings. The plugin now maintains Phpactor's global config file (~/.config/phpactor/phpactor.json) pointing at a STATIC index that only the plugin's offline build writes, while each server session works on its own live copy (a running session rewrites index records and corrupts any index it shares). Diagnostics now resolve project classes correctly at the source: no false findings, no red marks anywhere.
0.2.9
  • Fixed: corrupted index caused recurring "Class not found". The index warm-up ran concurrently with the language server, and Phpactor's on-disk index has no file locking — the two writers overwrote each other's records (classes ended up indexed with an empty file path, which re-broke diagnostics, editor marks and the project tree). The warm-up now completes synchronously before the server process starts, and the index is versioned anew (one clean rebuild).
0.2.8
  • Fixed: false "Class not found" still shown in the editor. LSP4IJ renders editor underlines through a highlighting pass that bypasses the inspection hook used by 0.2.7's filter — the suppression now also hooks createAnnotation, the common funnel of all diagnostic rendering paths.
0.2.7
  • Fixed: mass "Class X not found" false positives on non-Composer projects. Phpactor's diagnostics only resolve classes through a Composer autoloader (its fallback scanner follows no symlinks and requires file name == class name). The plugin now generates a Composer-compatible class map at every server start (~0.5s) and feeds it to Phpactor — plus filters the remaining false "not found" findings for classes that verifiably exist in the project. Real Composer projects are untouched.
  • Fixed: the index warm-up was a silent no-op — Phpactor's CLI rejects the nested JSON config format; it now sends flat keys, so the offline index build actually runs.
0.2.6
  • swoole_system / Swoole specialization. The Swoole extension's legacy runtime aliases (swoole_table, swoole_server, Co\*, …) are registered with class_alias() and are invisible to static analysis. The plugin now generates stub declarations for them (one file per namespace, next to the PHP stubs), so go-to-definition, completion and constant resolution work on legacy Swoole code, and the remaining false "Class … not found" diagnostics are filtered client-side for exactly those names.
0.2.5
  • Better protobuf support. Diagnostics are suppressed in generated pb_proto_*.php files (they only produced unfixable style noise), and the index size limit was raised so large generated files stay navigable.
  • Framework-ready indexing. The plugin now warms up Phpactor's index once per server start (offline index:build), so framework classes resolve immediately after opening a project instead of waiting for file events.
0.2.4
  • Fixed: Find Usages / "who calls this method" popup did nothing. Clicking a method declaration with Cmd+Click / Ctrl+Click never listed callers and Edit ▸ Find Usages found nothing. Root cause: LSP4IJ's target-element evaluator is registered with an empty language key, so the platform never consults it and a reference-free PSI like ours has no way to resolve the caret target. The plugin now registers its own evaluator for the PHP language, wiring the caret identifier into LSP4IJ's textDocument/references pipeline.
0.2.3
  • Fixed: no completion / wrong "Class not found" errors in symlink-based workspaces. Projects whose root is a container of symlinked checkouts (common with monorepo-style setups) now index correctly — Phpactor's indexer follows symlinks, and the on-disk index is versioned so the broken one is rebuilt once automatically.
  • Fixed: editor errors after toggling the LSP4IJ plugin. The PHP language and its token types are now attached to this plugin's main descriptor, so disabling or reloading LSP4IJ no longer breaks highlighting with "Trying to access element type from unloaded plugin" errors.
0.2.2
  • Added a plugin icon (shown in the Plugins list and on the Marketplace).
0.2.1
  • Refreshed the file/SDK icon to a cleaner monospace php mark.
0.2.0
  • PHP code intelligence. Completion, go-to-definition, hover documentation and error highlighting — powered by a local PHP language server (Phpactor) that runs on the portable PHP interpreter. Fully offline; no Node.js or system install. Requires the free LSP4IJ plugin. Active on IDEs without built-in PHP (IDEA Community, GoLand, …); on PhpStorm the native PHP support is used instead.
  • One-click setup. A banner on your first .php file offers Enable code intelligence: it downloads Phpactor automatically and takes you straight to the Plugins screen to install LSP4IJ — no hunting for what's needed.
  • Jump into PHP built-ins. Go-to-definition works on standard PHP functions and classes (\DateTime, json_encode, …) via bundled stubs.
  • Run Composer with portable PHP. Right-click ▸ Run Composer (Portable PHP) to run install / update / dump-autoload / require and more in a console — no system PHP or Composer required.
0.1.3
  • Forward compatibility: dropped an internal-only platform API and the platform APIs scheduled for removal in newer IDE builds (verified with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier). No functional changes.
0.1.2
  • Maintenance: replaced an internal-only platform API with its public equivalent and updated deprecated icon-loading calls, for forward compatibility with newer IDE builds. No functional changes.
0.1.1
  • Works alongside PhpStorm & IDEA Ultimate. No longer clashes with the bundled PHP plugin: the editor language support quietly steps aside where PHP is already supported, while the portable interpreter, run action, and setup tools keep working in every IDE.
  • Batteries-included PHP. Downloaded interpreters now bundle ~65 extensions (intl, gd, soap, curl, zip, sodium, mbstring, and more), so composer install and real-world projects run without hitting a missing-extension error.
  • Clearer run action. The run configuration is now named "PHP Script (Portable)" so it's easy to tell apart from PhpStorm's built-in "PHP Script".
  • Clearer settings. The interpreter settings page is now Settings ▸ Languages & Frameworks ▸ Portable PHP, so it no longer looks like a duplicate of PhpStorm's own PHP settings.
